quote: **The NJ Rehabilitation Subcode** does not count a coating as a roof covering layer, so **roof coating** preserves the overlay allowance, while **roof replacement** by tear-off resets the layer count, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4.
issue: Unsupported code interpretation pinned to a named regulation. The pack for N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4 (facts-nj-regulatory-climate.md lines 61-65) lists only the full-removal triggers: covering water-soaked/deteriorated, covering is wood shake/slate/clay/cement/asbestos-cement tile, or 'two or more applications of any roof covering already exist.' No pack text states a liquid-applied coating is exempt from the layer count or 'preserves the overlay allowance' — a coating is arguably itself 'an application of roof covering.' This is false-precision attribution: a definitive compliance claim pinned to a regulation that does not state it. The same unsupported assertion is mirrored in comparisonRows[7] itemA ('Not counted as a roof covering layer' under feature 'NJ code layer count (N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4)').
fix: njSpecific.content[0] — Before: 'The NJ Rehabilitation Subcode does not count a coating as a roof covering layer, so roof coating preserves the overlay allowance, while roof replacement by tear-off resets the layer count, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4.' After: '**Roof coating** renews a sound membrane without a tear-off, so it does not trigger the Rehabilitation Subcode full-removal rules, while **roof replacement** by tear-off resets the layer count — N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4 requires full removal once a covering is water-soaked, deteriorated, or two layers deep.' Mirror in comparisonRows[7] itemA — Before: 'Not counted as a roof covering layer' → After: 'No tear-off; renews existing membrane'.
refuteReason: Confirmed against facts-nj-regulatory-climate.md lines 61-65: N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4 lists full-removal triggers (water-soaked/deteriorated, listed covering types, or two-or-more applications) and contains NO 'coating is not a layer' or 'preserves the overlay allowance' provision. The exemption claim is invented and pinned to a named regulation it cannot support — exactly the false-precision attribution the review targets.

quote: coating over saturated insulation traps that moisture and accelerates deck rot, per ASTM C1153 and InterNACHI.
issue: ASTM C1153 is over-scoped. Per facts-materials-economics.md §7 (lines 384-389), ASTM C1153 governs ONLY infrared location of wet insulation and core-cut/probe/moisture-meter verification — it says nothing about coating trapping moisture or accelerating deck rot. The trailing 'per ASTM C1153 and InterNACHI' wrongly extends the standards-body pin past the detection clause onto the causal trapped-moisture/deck-rot clause. (Note: contrary to the reviewer, InterNACHI IS a valid named source for the causal half — facts-components-specialty.md line 274 attributes 'Trapped moisture decays sheathing' to InterNACHI [PRIMARY] — so InterNACHI stays; only ASTM C1153 must be re-scoped to detection.)
fix: Before: '...wet insulation holds heat and shows as warm anomalies after sunset under ASTM C1153, verified by core cut, and coating over saturated insulation traps that moisture and accelerates deck rot, per ASTM C1153 and InterNACHI.' After: '...wet insulation holds heat and shows as warm anomalies after sunset under ASTM C1153, verified by core cut; coating over saturated insulation seals that moisture in, where trapped moisture decays the deck, per InterNACHI.' (Keeps the fact; scopes ASTM C1153 to detection only and retains the correct InterNACHI pin for the decay clause.)
refuteReason: Confirmed against facts-materials-economics.md lines 384-389: ASTM C1153 = 'Location of Wet Insulation … Using Infrared Imaging' + core-cut verification only — it does NOT cover trapped-moisture deck rot, so pinning the causal clause to it is over-attribution. The InterNACHI half is corrected (not stripped) because facts-components-specialty.md line 274 explicitly names InterNACHI [PRIMARY] for 'Trapped moisture decays sheathing.'
